problem: Development was slowed again by 19 active/in-progress and 11 queued GitHub Actions runs despite prior queue-storm controls.
root_cause: Obsolete-run identity detection existed, but queued obsolete runs waited six hours, obsolete in-progress runs waited thirty minutes, the supervisor ran every fifteen minutes, and recovery dispatch stayed enabled until twenty non-terminal runs. Proven-obsolete work therefore retained scarce runner capacity far longer than necessary.
prevention: Cancel only runs whose exact SHA/PR/branch identity proves they are obsolete; never cancel healthy current-head work merely to reduce counts.
Once queued work is proven obsolete, make it cancellation-eligible after 60 seconds rather than hours.
Once in-progress work is proven obsolete, make it cancellation-eligible after 300 seconds.
Run the single-flight recovery supervisor every five minutes so stale capacity is drained promptly.
Allow up to 100 proven-obsolete cancellations per cycle so a large stale backlog can be reduced in one bounded pass.
Open the recovery dispatch circuit at 12 total non-terminal runs so recovery never amplifies saturation.
Regression-test the exact cadence, thresholds and identity-driven cancellation controls.
Persist the same invariant in the canonical delivery-concurrency skill.
failed_approaches: Treating stale capacity as an age-only cleanup problem with six-hour queued and thirty-minute in-progress grace periods.
Letting the recovery supervisor wait fifteen minutes between cleanup opportunities while development is saturated.
Allowing recovery dispatch until twenty non-terminal runs even though lower pressure already delays protected delivery.
